newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Trial of 128 Red Terror suspects opens in Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: Trial of 128 Red Terror suspects opens in Ethiopia.

text.p: The trial of Olympic marathon gold medallist Mamo Wolde and 127 others charged with crimes during the 1970s Red Terror campaign in Ethiopia opened on Monday.

The 128 were allegedly involved in crimes in the capital Addis Ababa during the campaign, in which tens of thousands of opponents of the military regime which seized power in 1977 were killed and tortured.
The accused also included a former president of Addis Ababa Univeristy, Professor Alemayheu Tefera Mesheshsa.

Charge documents said that all the defendants served as members of Wereda (District 16) administration and participated in "aggravated genocide"; that they coordinated "revolutionary campaigns" and were members of Red Terror committees.
They were also accused of the arbitrary detention of members of the Ethiopian Peoples Revolutionary Party, a Marxist opposition group, torture, inflicting suffering and killings.
The court accepted the defendants' plea to study the charges before responding. The trial was adjourned to April 14.
The defendants are charged under Ethiopian Penal Code of 1957 and face the death penalty if found guilty.

The government has charged a total of 5,198 people with war crimes, aggravated homicide and genocide. Of these 1,200 are suspected of invovlment in the Red Terrror campaign during the rule of ousted Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam.
Some defendants, like Mamo Wolde, 65, who took golds at the 1968 and 1972 Games, were detained for several years before they were finally charged.
Mengistu fled after he was ousted in May 1991 and lives in exile in Zimbabwe.
